text: The B.S. in Computer Engineering (2025-2026) requires 126 hours (45 in residence, last semester at UTD) with a minimum 2.0 GPA. A grade of C or better is required in CS 1436, CE 1337, CE 2305, and CE 2336, and a grade of C- or better in all other courses on the degree plan. Major Preparatory Requirements (37 or 41 hours), Major Core Requirements (44 hours), and Technical Electives (11 hours) count toward the Major GPA; the plan also includes 24 hours of Remaining State Core Curriculum and Free Electives.
source_title: B.S. in Computer Engineering Degree Plan (2025-2026)
section_heading: B.S. in Computer Engineering (2025-2026): Graduation and Grade Requirements

text: The B.S. in Computer Engineering (2025-2026) major introductory courses are taken in the first year in college only; transfer students substitute an upper level technical elective. They are ECS 1100 Intro to Engineering and CS (1 hour) and CE 1100 Intro to Computer Engineering I (1 hour). The lower-division Major Preparatory Requirements (Major GPA) total 37 or 41 hours: MATH 2413 or MATH 2417 Differential Calculus or Calculus I (4 hours); CS 1436 Programming Fundamentals (4 hours, C or better); CE 1202 Intro to Computer Engineering II (2 hours); CE 2310 Introduction to Digital Systems (3 hours); CE 1337 Computer Science I (3 hours, C or better); MATH 2414 or MATH 2419 Integral Calculus or Calculus II (4 hours); PHYS 2325 Mechanics (3 hours); PHYS 2125 Physics Laboratory I (1 hour); ENGR 2300 Linear Algebra for Engineers (3 hours); MATH 2415 Calculus of Several Variables (4 hours; not needed if the student has completed MATH 2419); MATH 2420 Differential Equations w/ Applications (4 hours); PHYS 2326 Electromagnetism and Waves (3 hours); PHYS 2126 Physics Laboratory II (1 hour); CE 2336 or CS 2337 Computer Science II (JAVA or C++) (3 hours, C or better); and CE 2305 Discrete Mathematics for Computing I (3 hours, C or better).
source_title: B.S. in Computer Engineering Degree Plan (2025-2026)
section_heading: Major Introductory Courses and Major Preparatory Requirements

text: The B.S. in Computer Engineering (2025-2026) lower/upper-division Major Core Requirements (Major GPA) total 44 hours: ENGR 3341 Probability Theory & Statistics (3 hours); CE 3201 CE Fundamentals Lab I (2 hours); CE 2301 Electrical Network Analysis (3 hours); CE 3345 Data Structures & Intro to Algorithmic Analysis (3 hours); CE 3320 Digital Circuits (3 hours); CE 3202 CE Fundamentals Lab II (2 hours); CE 3311 Electronic Circuits (3 hours); CE 3354 Software Engineering (3 hours); CE 3303 Signals and Systems (3 hours); CE 3161 Social Issues and Ethics in Engineering (1 hour); ECS 2390 Professional & Technical Communication (3 hours); CE 4304 Computer Architecture (3 hours); CE 4370 Embedded Systems (3 hours); CE 4348 Operating Systems Concepts (3 hours); CE 4388 Senior Design Project I (3 hours); and CE 4389 Senior Design Project II (3 hours).
source_title: B.S. in Computer Engineering Degree Plan (2025-2026)

text: The B.S. in Computer Engineering (2025-2026) Technical Electives (Major GPA) total 11 hours: a CE Elective Lab (2 hours, chosen from a list of options); a MATH Technical Elective (3 hours, chosen from a list of options); and two Technical Electives at the EE/CE/CS 4XXX level (3 hours each). Free Electives consist of a 3-hour Free Elective and a 1-hour Free Elective, both of which are not needed if the student has MATH 2413.
source_title: B.S. in Computer Engineering Degree Plan (2025-2026)

text: The B.S. in Computer Engineering (2025-2026) lower-division Remaining State Core Curriculum totals 24 hours: RHET 1302 for Communication (Core: 010) (3 hours); GOVT 2305 and GOVT 2306 for Government/Political Science (Core: 070) (3 hours each); two American History (Core: 060) courses (3 hours each, chosen from a list of options); one Language, Philosophy and Culture (Core: 040) course (3 hours); one Creative Arts (Core: 050) course (3 hours); and one Social Behavioral Science (Core: 080) course (3 hours).
source_title: B.S. in Computer Engineering Degree Plan (2025-2026)
